newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH GOVT RE-INTRODUCES RETAIL OPEN HOURS BILL.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH GOVT RE-INTRODUCES RETAIL OPEN HOURS BILL.

text.p: The government on Monday sent to parliament for the second time a proposal to liberalise shop opening hours to include Sunday trading, taking the first step towards a vote of confidence in February.
A spokesman at the prime minister's office said the retail store opening hours bill had been formally forwarded to parliament at the presidential audience.

Parliament on December 19 defeated the bill by 84 votes to 82. Angered by the surprise setback, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said another vote in February on the same bill will also be a confidence vote in his government.
Parliament is scheduled to reconvene on February 3 after the Christmas recess.
In December, 36 of the five government parties' 142 MPs voted against the proposal. Of those, 20 were from Lipponen's own Social Democratic Party.
Some leading government party politicians said the many absentees -- 30 MPs in all -- were to blame for the defeat.
But political analysts said the Lipponen cabinet's first significant setback in parliament had been an indication of growing criticism among left-wing MPs of right-leaning fiscal austerity policies.
Lipponen's decision to turn the issue into a vote of confidence has been strongly criticised by some SDP MPs, many of whom have close ties to Finland's influential trade unions.
Some other unions quietly support the shop workers' union, which is fiercely opposed to allowing retail stores to be open on Sundays, as proposed by the government.
Union support is crucial for the government to succeed in its drive to take Finland into the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union from the start in 1999, analysts say.
Left-leaning MPs are not expected to vote in parliament in favour of Finland joining EMU if the trade unions oppose entry.
Nevertheless, the left-right-green coalition's broad majority in the 200-seat legislature is widely expected to ensure that it will easily win the confidence vote on the retail opening hours issue.
Lipponen's government has won four votes of confidence since taking office in April 1995.
